title: Toast
description: Temporary notifications with a title, a description and a semantic color, shown with toast() from anywhere (no React context needed) and rendered by a ToastProvider inside your app tree, so they inherit your app's context (theme, locale). Loading toasts, promise tracking, in-place updates, actions and a maximum count are built in. Server rendering is safe.

usage.title: When to use which: useToast() or toast()
usage.hook: Inside components, call useToast(): the toasts it shows follow the nearest ConfigProvider scope. Under a nested provider they are rendered into its portal host, with its theme, palette and tokens, and their built-in labels use its language. The owning ToastProvider still renders them, with its position, max and labels.
usage.function: Outside React (event buses, API clients, stores and other non-component modules), import toast() directly: no hook is available there, and its toasts use the scope of the ToastProvider, usually the root theme and language.
usage.modal: While a modal dialog is open (Modal, Drawer, ConfirmDialog, Command, a modal Popover or Menu), its hide-others treatment covers the toast viewport like the rest of the page: the viewport gets aria-hidden="true" and assistive technologies only see the dialog until it closes. <minerva-toast-region> behaves the same way (opt out on a region with data-minerva-keep-visible).

wc:minerva-toast-region.summary: Toast stack (viewport) rendering the toasts of the `toast()` API.
wc:minerva-toast-region.description: Toast region (the React library's `ToastProvider` viewport): renders the toasts shown with the `toast()` API, stacked at `position`, with the same DOM, classes, roles and keyboard behaviour as React. - Each toast is a live region: `role="status"`, or `role="alert"` for danger toasts (loading toasts stay a polite status). The stack is a `role="region"` labelled "Notifications (F8)" (localized). - Toasts close after `duration` (default 4000 ms; loading toasts stay open); the countdown pauses while a toast is hovered or holds focus. - The hotkey (F8 by default) moves focus to the region; Escape closes the focused toast; closing a focused toast moves focus to the next toast, else back where it came from (never to `<body>`). - Toasts without an explicit region render in the first connected region (document order); `toast.region(el)` / `{ region }` target another one, e.g. inside a `<minerva-config>` scope (its theme and language apply). When `toast()` runs with no region on the page, one is appended to `<body>` (and removed again when a page region connects). - The stack is shown in the top layer (Popover API, `popover="manual"`) and raised again when a toast appears or a Minerva overlay opens, so toasts stay above modals and stay clickable. Like the React library's `ToastProvider` viewport, the region is treated like any other page content by a modal's hide-others: while a modal dialog (modal, drawer, confirm, command, modal popover / menu) is open, the region (or its ancestor next to the dialog) gets `aria-hidden="true"` and assistive technologies only see the dialog; it is exposed again when the dialog closes. Opt out on a given region with the `data-minerva-keep-visible` attribute (core's hide-others never hides such elements).

basic.title: Basic usage
basic.description: Success shows Saved, Danger shows Request failed, Warning shows Unsaved changes and Info shows New version. Keep at most three notifications.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: color picks the semantic color: info (default), success, warning or danger. It sets the accent, the icon and the role: danger is announced as an alert, the others as a status.

options.title: Options
options.description: toast({ color, title, description, duration }) for full control; duration 0 keeps the toast until it is closed. toast.dismiss(id) closes one toast, toast.dismiss() all of them. Hovering or focusing a toast pauses its timer.

loading.title: Loading, update and promise
loading.description: toast.loading (or the loading: true option, with any color) shows a spinner instead of the icon and stays open; toast.update(id, { loading: false, ... }) turns it into a result in place. toast.promise(promise, { loading, success, error }) does both for a promise.

action.title: Action, icon and onClose
action.description: action adds a button (e.g. Undo) that also closes the toast; icon replaces the color icon; closable: false hides the close button; onClose runs once when the toast closes.

dedupe.title: Same id replaces
dedupe.description: Showing a toast with the id of a visible one replaces it and restarts its timer, instead of stacking duplicates (handy for polling errors).

scoped.title: Scoped: useToast() vs toast()
scoped.description: Both buttons sit in a nested ConfigProvider (dark theme, tech palette, Chinese). useToast() renders its toast inside that scope (dark tokens, Chinese close label, its own viewport at the same position); toast() renders at the root, with the page theme and language.

keyboard.title: Keyboard
keyboard.description: F8 (the hotkey prop, also announced in the region label "Notifications (F8)") moves focus to the toasts. Escape dismisses the focused toast; after closing one, focus moves to the next toast's close button, then back to where it was before entering the toasts.

ToastOptions.id: Identifier of the toast; generated when omitted. Showing a toast with the id of a visible one replaces it (and restarts its timer) instead of stacking a duplicate
ToastOptions.color: Semantic color of the toast; sets its accent, icon and ARIA role (danger is announced as an alert, the others as a status)
ToastOptions.loading: Shows a spinner instead of the icon and keeps the toast open (duration defaults to 0) until it is updated or dismissed; announced as a status
ToastOptions.title: Main text
ToastOptions.duration: Time in milliseconds before the toast closes automatically; 0 keeps it open. Loading toasts default to 0
ToastOptions.icon: Replaces the color icon (or the loading spinner); null hides it
ToastOptions.action: Action button rendered in the toast (e.g. Undo)
ToastOptions.onClose: Called once with the toast id when it closes, whatever the reason

ToastAction.label: Visible text of the button
ToastAction.onClick: Called when the button is activated, before the toast closes

ToastProviderProps.children: Application content; the toast viewport is rendered after it
ToastProviderProps.max: Maximum number of toasts shown at once; when exceeded the oldest close first
ToastProviderProps.pauseOnHover: Pauses the auto-close timer while a toast is hovered or focused
ToastProviderProps.aria-label: Accessible label of the toast region, used as is (the default one includes the hotkey)
ToastProviderProps.closeLabel: Accessible label of the close buttons
ToastProviderProps.hotkey: Keys pressed together to move focus to the toast region (the first one holding toasts): key codes (F8, KeyT), keys or modifiers (altKey, ctrlKey, metaKey, shiftKey). Shown in the default region label, e.g. "Notifications (F8)"; an empty array disables it

ToastApi.info: Shows an info toast with the given title
ToastApi.success: Shows a success toast with the given title
ToastApi.warning: Shows a warning toast with the given title
ToastApi.danger: Shows a danger toast with the given title
ToastApi.loading: Shows a loading toast (spinner, no auto-close) with the given title
ToastApi.promise: Shows a loading toast while the promise is pending, then turns it into a success or danger toast; returns the given promise
ToastApi.update: Changes an open toast in place (merging the options) and restarts its timer; loading: false turns a loading toast into a regular one (with the default duration unless one is given). Unknown ids are ignored
ToastApi.dismiss: Closes the toast with the given id, or every toast when omitted

ToastPromiseMessages.loading: Title while the promise is pending
ToastPromiseMessages.success: Title once the promise resolves (a node, or a function of the value)
ToastPromiseMessages.error: Title once the promise rejects (a node, or a function of the error)

cssVars.--toast-width: Width of the toast stack (capped by the viewport)
cssVars.--toast-offset: Distance between the stack and the viewport edges
cssVars.--toast-radius: Corner radius of a toast (defaults to --radius-md)
cssVars.--toast-background: Base background of a toast (under the color tint)
cssVars.--toast-z-index: Stacking order of the stack (defaults to --z-toast)
cssVars.--toast-icon-background: Background of the round chip behind the status icon (defaults to the color's accent at 14%)

native.limitations: On Native, top-left/top-center/top-right map to a full-width top stack; bottom-left/bottom-center/bottom-right map to a bottom stack. Message actions and the maximum count match the web example; horizontal corner placement does not.
